text:
Boston gave Utah two first-round picks for JJ Peterka in June, and the early return is steady rather than loud: six goals and 15 points in 22 games, on about 17 and a half minutes a night.

The shooting is the story. "Every time JJ Peterka shoots, you're reminded why he should shoot more," Ty Anderson of 98.5 The Sports Hub posted on Nov 19. His own chances are up to 1.07 expected goals per 60 from 0.73 last season, and six goals on 6.8 expected is right on track. The night he fired seven shots on Florida, Nov 8, he scored.

He moves, too. NHL Edge has him at 66 bursts over 20 mph, 96th percentile among forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him leaving his own zone with possession on 59% of his exits last season.

At five on five Boston breaks about even with him on and off the ice, which is fine but not yet what two firsts are meant to buy.

What to watch: he went three straight games without a goal before scoring in Detroit on Nov 18. The volume is what separates his good nights from his quiet ones.
headline: Peterka should shoot more, and everyone knows it
